newsitem.title: GERMANY: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST -JUNE 23.
newsitem.headline: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST -JUNE 23.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising,
Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and
Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
MUNICH - Commercial TV channels Sat.1 and Pro Sieben may have to
pay up to 16.3 million marks ($9.4 million) in fines because
they
broadcast too many commercials, news magazine Focus reports.
Last week a German court fined RTL 20 million marks for
interrupting feature films too frequently with ads.(Focus)
FRANKFURT - Kronberg-based Public Relations Partners has been
named to handle all public relations and publicity work for the
Hassia und Luisen mineral water group. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
MUNICH - German media firm Leo Kirch agrees to buy an extra 37.5
percent stake in pay TV channel Premiere from its current French
holder,
Canal Plus, German magazine Focus says in its weekend edition.
The stake, which Focus says is worth around one billion marks,
will bring Kirch's total holding in Premiere up to 62.5
percent.
(Reuter)
HAMBURG - Germany's weekly Spiegel magazine says Thomas
Middelhoff is due to take over as chairman of the German media
giant Bertelsmann AG in October 1998. Formerly a
company
board member in charge of corporate development and multimedia,
Middelhoff will be presented by current chairman Mark Woessner
at a management meeting on July 5 as his successor, the Spiegel
report says.
(Reuter)
FRANKFURT - ProSieben, Germany's first television broadcaster to
seek a public listing for its shares, is likely to set an
ambitious
bookbuilding range when it gives details of its offering next
week,
analysts believe. The strong relative performance of comparable
European media stocks in recent weeks, coupled with hopes for a
high degree of retail investor interest, will encourage the
firm
to target issue proceeds of close to 1.4 billion marks, they
estimate.
(Reuter)
LUDWIGSHAFEN - Media authorities have called on Deutsche
Telekom to make a further two channels available on its
country-wide cable network.(Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
FRANKFURT - Klaus Wiegandt, head of retail group Metro AG has
lashed out against what he sees as the tough price competition
in the
sector, talking of "a policy of destroying added value". He
believes
overcapacity among producers lies behind the pressure on
retailers
to lower their prices.
(Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Consumer goods group Procter & Gamble (P&G) says
recent efficiency measures have been proved correct by an
increase in market share by its major brands. Costs have been
cut by more than 100 million marks in a recent savings drive.
(Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
BONN - Deutsche Telekom AG denies a report that it plans to
dismiss one of its board members, Herbert May, in the next few
weeks.
Germany's weekly Spiegel magazine says in its latest edition
that May will be dismissed after talks over allowing other
telecommunications firms access to Deutsche's network broke
down.
(Reuter)
MUNICH - TV presenter Ulla Kock am Brink is switching from the
RTL channel to the rival ProSieben. She will begin work for her
new employers at the start of next year. RTL shows hosted by
Kock
am Brink include "Verzeih mir" (Excuse Me!) and the long-running
"100.000 Mark Show" (Reuter)
